parameters.description: Which days to sum up. Each is compared with the same number of days just before it: last week (Monday to Sunday) with the week before, last month with the month before. Days are counted in the property's time zone, up to and including yesterday. Leave blank for the last 7 days.
parameters.name: period

new_users.description: How many people visited for the first time in the period, a plain number.

new_users_change.description: The change from the period before, as a percentage to one decimal place, such as 12.5 or -3.0. Empty when the period before had none.

new_users_change_display.description: The change in words, such as "up 12.5%", "down 3.0%", "no change", or "new this period" when the period before had none, so it reads well after the number: "12,480 (up 12.5%)".

new_users_display.description: The same number of people visited for the first time with thousands separators, such as 12,480, ready to put in a message.

new_users_previous.description: How many people visited for the first time in the period before it, of the same length, a plain number.

page_views.description: How many pages were viewed in the period, a plain number.

page_views_change.description: The change from the period before, as a percentage to one decimal place, such as 12.5 or -3.0. Empty when the period before had none.

page_views_change_display.description: The change in words, such as "up 12.5%", "down 3.0%", "no change", or "new this period" when the period before had none, so it reads well after the number: "12,480 (up 12.5%)".

page_views_display.description: The same number of pages were viewed with thousands separators, such as 12,480, ready to put in a message.

page_views_previous.description: How many pages were viewed in the period before it, of the same length, a plain number.

period.description: The period chosen, such as last_week.

period_display.description: The period ready to read, such as Nov 3 – Nov 9, 2026.

period_end.description: The period's last day, such as 2026-11-09.

period_start.description: The period's first day, such as 2026-11-03.

previous_period_display.description: The period it is compared with, ready to read, such as Oct 27 – Nov 2, 2026.

previous_period_end.description: The last day of the period it is compared with, such as 2026-11-02.

previous_period_start.description: The first day of the period it is compared with, such as 2026-10-27.

sessions.description: How many visits (sessions) there were in the period, a plain number.

sessions_change.description: The change from the period before, as a percentage to one decimal place, such as 12.5 or -3.0. Empty when the period before had none.

sessions_change_display.description: The change in words, such as "up 12.5%", "down 3.0%", "no change", or "new this period" when the period before had none, so it reads well after the number: "12,480 (up 12.5%)".

sessions_display.description: The same number of visits (sessions) there were with thousands separators, such as 12,480, ready to put in a message.

sessions_previous.description: How many visits (sessions) there were in the period before it, of the same length, a plain number.

top_pages.description: The five most viewed pages in the period, most first.

page_path.description: The page's address after the domain, such as /pricing.

page_title.description: The page's title, such as Pricing.

views.description: How many times it was viewed.

views_display.description: The views with thousands separators, such as 4,210.

top_pages_text.description: Beta. The top pages as numbered lines ready to post, one per page, such as "1. Home (/): 4,210 views"; empty when no page was viewed.

users.description: How many people visited (Users in Google Analytics) in the period, a plain number.

users_change.description: The change from the period before, as a percentage to one decimal place, such as 12.5 or -3.0. Empty when the period before had none.

users_change_display.description: The change in words, such as "up 12.5%", "down 3.0%", "no change", or "new this period" when the period before had none, so it reads well after the number: "12,480 (up 12.5%)".

users_display.description: The same number of people visited (Users in Google Analytics) with thousands separators, such as 12,480, ready to put in a message.

users_previous.description: How many people visited (Users in Google Analytics) in the period before it, of the same length, a plain number.

output.custom: true for an event of your own, false for one Google defines.
